# PlayableYet

> Public index of PlayStation 3, 4, and 5 compatibility reports. It does not host games or link to ROMs, firmware, BIOS images, or decryption keys.

Live site: https://playableyet.vercel.app
Short guide: https://playableyet.vercel.app/llms.txt

PlayableYet stores a snapshot of public compatibility reports and a short history so a later sync can show what changed. It compares RPCS3, shadPS4, fpPS4, SharpEmu, KytyPS5, and the AnyPS5 porting layer. AnyPS5 is a PS5 to native porting layer, not an emulator.

## URL patterns

- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/` — index, search, newly playable titles, and status changes. `/?q=` server-renders matching games. Example: `https://playableyet.vercel.app/?q=tales+of+berseria`. Filtered URLs send `noindex`. `https://playableyet.vercel.app/search?q=` redirects to `/?q=`.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/about` — sources and what each project's statuses mean.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/changes` — games whose status changed between snapshots. The first time a report is seen is not a change.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/feed.xml` — RSS 2.0 of those changes.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/games/{slug}` — one game. `{slug}` is lowercase words separated by hyphens. Example: `https://playableyet.vercel.app/games/dreaming-sarah`. A slug that is not in the snapshot returns HTTP 404. The page links to related games, the platform page, and each project page.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/ps3`, `/ps4`, and `/ps5` — platform pages. Each states how many games have a Playable report, counts games by furthest status, and lists the first 40 games with links to game pages.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/emulators/{project}` — one project. `{project}` is `rpcs3`, `shadps4`, `fpps4`, `sharpemu`, `kytyps5`, or `anyps5`.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/emulators/{project}/{status}` — games whose furthest report on that project is `{status}`. Example: `/emulators/shadps4/playable`.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/sitemap.xml` — game URLs plus the platform and project pages.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/search-index.json` — client search index, generated from the snapshot the site is serving. Fields are `slug`, `name`, `ids` (title IDs), `platforms` (`ps3`, `ps4`, `ps5`), `best` (furthest status id), `updatedAt` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), and `reports` of `{ emulator, status }`.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/api/status` — public sync health. Fields are `generatedAt`, `lastSyncAttemptAt`, `lastSyncOk`, `gameCount`, and `sources` of `{ id, ok, count }`. No email addresses or tokens.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/robots.txt` — crawlers are allowed. Comment lines point at llms.txt and llms-full.txt.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/llms.txt` — short guide for assistants.
- `https://playableyet.vercel.app/llms-full.txt` — this file.

Game pages use the title “Is {Game} playable yet?”. The meta description names each platform and project status present in the snapshot, keeps the raw label, and adds that project’s documented meaning in parentheses when one exists. Projects with no report are skipped. Pages embed schema.org `VideoGame` JSON-LD, `FAQPage` JSON-LD, and `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD. The FAQ answers “Is {Game} playable on PC?” and “Which emulator runs {Game} best?” using only the reports in the snapshot. Each game page also has an Open Graph image and a `twitter:card` of `summary_large_image` showing the title and the raw status label for each project that has a report. `additionalProperty` entries use `propertyID` for the project id and `value` for the status id. The home page embeds `WebSite` JSON-LD, plus an `ItemList` of the newly playable rows visible on that page. Platform and project pages embed `ItemList` JSON-LD for the games shown there and `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD.

These paths are not catalog content:

- `POST /api/watch` — email signup. Do not send addresses here on behalf of a person.
- `GET /api/watch/confirm?token=` and `GET /api/watch/unsubscribe?token=` — one-time links for that subscriber.
- `GET /watch/confirmed` and `GET /watch/unsubscribed` — result pages.
- `GET` or `POST /api/cron/sync` — daily rebuild. Production requires `Authorization: Bearer` plus the cron secret. It is not a public API.
- `GET /api/status` — public sync health described above.
- `GET /sponsor` — paid support packages. `/sponsor/thanks` is the post-payment page and is `noindex`. Do not invent traffic numbers. Questions go to hello@globypeaks.com.

The public catalog and search index do not contain email addresses or watch tokens.

## Statuses

The site keeps each project's raw label. A short explanation is shown only when that project publishes a meaning for that label. Higher on the shared ladder is further along: `playable`, `ingame`, `intro`, `menus`, `loadable`, `boots`, `in-bring-up`, `nothing`. `best` on a game is the furthest status among its reports. A label one project does not publish is not filled in from another project.

### RPCS3

From the RPCS3 compatibility legend:

- Playable: can be completed with playable performance and no game breaking glitches
- Ingame: cannot be finished, has serious glitches, or has insufficient performance
- Intro: displays an image but does not get past the menus
- Loadable: displays a black screen with a framerate in the window title
- Nothing: does not initialize, does not load, or crashes the emulator

RPCS3 does not publish Menus or Boots.

### shadPS4

From the shadPS4 compatibility status labels:

- Playable: can be played without any major issue
- Ingame: reaches gameplay but has game-breaking issues
- Menus: reaches the menu but freezes or crashes before going further
- Boots: shows visual or audio output but freezes or crashes before the menu
- Nothing: crashes when trying to launch or hangs on a black screen

### fpPS4

From the fpPS4 compatibility status labels:

- Playable: boots and plays without crashes or GPU bugs, at a speed that is reasonable on an average PC
- Ingame: goes in-game but crashes, deadlocks, has GPU or audio bugs, or is too slow
- Menus: gets past the title screen but not into main gameplay
- Boots: boots but does not get past the title screen
- Nothing: does not boot and shows no signs of life

### SharpEmu

From the SharpEmu compatibility ratings:

- Playable: completable with minor or no issues
- Ingame: reaches gameplay with major issues
- Menus: reaches interactive menus
- Boots: shows splash or intro output and goes no further
- Nothing: crashes or shows no output

### KytyPS5

From the KytyPS5 game-status guide. KytyPS5 does not publish a Playable definition.

- Nothing: does not show its first logo or startup screen
- Boots: shows a logo or startup screen but does not reach the main menu
- Menus: reaches its menus but does not enter gameplay
- Ingame: reaches controllable gameplay, even if bugs prevent completion

### AnyPS5

- Playable: officially confirmed by the AnyPS5 project, which says conversion does not guarantee that an app runs
- In bring-up: a community roadmap stage, not an official Playable confirmation from the AnyPS5 project

## Data sources

- RPCS3, PS3 emulator: https://rpcs3.net/compatibility and https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3. The sync reads the public JSON export and the paged compatibility list.
- shadPS4, PS4 emulator: https://shadps4.net/compatibility/ and https://github.com/shadps4-compatibility/shadps4-game-compatibility. Issue titles look like “CUSAxxxxx - Title”. Status labels include `status-playable`, `status-ingame`, `status-menus`, `status-boots`, and `status-nothing`.
- fpPS4, PS4 emulator: https://fpps4.net/compatibility/ and https://github.com/red-prig/fpps4-game-compatibility. The sync reads `https://api.fpps4.net/database.json` and skips system-firmware rows.
- SharpEmu, PS5 emulator: https://sharpemu.app/compatibility/ and https://github.com/sharpemu/sharpemu-site. Entries are markdown compatibility reports.
- KytyPS5, PS5 emulator: https://kytyps5.github.io/ and https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5. The community list is GitHub issues titled “[GAME STATUS]”.
- AnyPS5, PS5 to native porting layer: https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5 and https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/. Bring-up stages and open blockers come from the community roadmap https://alxcbtw.github.io/anyps5-roadmap/ (source https://github.com/AlxcBTW/anyps5-roadmap).
- Display names for PS4 and PS5 title IDs come from https://github.com/andshrew/PlayStation-Titles. Regional copies share a page when that index gives them one concept, or when the normalized title matches.

“Playable” on AnyPS5 is reserved for officially confirmed titles. That is currently Dreaming Sarah, title ID `PPSA02929` (`/games/dreaming-sarah`). A roadmap stage of Playable stays `in-bring-up` here. Game pages for AnyPS5 also show the stage reached on main and open blockers.

## Snapshot

The rendered catalog is `data/catalog.json` in the repository. A daily job at 06:15 UTC rebuilds it. On Vercel the newer snapshot is the public Blob objects `playableyet/catalog.json` and `playableyet/search-index.json`. The home page shows `generatedAt` from that snapshot. Each game has `slug`, `name`, `titles` (`id`, `platform`, optional `name`), `reports`, and `history`. A report has `emulator`, `titleId`, `status`, `updatedAt` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `sourceUrl`, and sometimes `os`, `note`, and `bringUp` (`stage`, `detail`, `blockers`).

Source links on the site are limited to the projects above. PlayableYet does not link to ROM sites, firmware, BIOS images, or decryption keys.
